Bundesliga The anticipation was palpable as both sides looked to make their mark on the game, setting the stage for a compelling battle on the pitch. On 16 August 2026, Hertha BSC and 1. FC Heidenheim faced off in a match that demanded both tactical discipline and physical intensity. A whirlwind start The match exploded into life almost immediately. Hertha BSC asserted dominance early on, with Sebastian Groenning firing home after just 2 minutes, courtesy of an assist from Marten Winkler . The hosts did not relent, as Marten Winkler turned from provider to scorer in the 26th minute, followed by Deyovaisio Zeefuik extending the lead to three in the 35th minute. With Winkler proving to be the architect of the first half, the home side looked comfortable heading into the break. Tactical shift and recovery The second half saw a revitalized 1. FC Heidenheim emerge from the tunnel with clear intent to change their fortunes. Their efforts were rewarded in the 49th minute when Jan Schoeppner found the back of the net, set up by Mikkel Kaufmann . The game became increasingly testy as the clock ticked down, with disciplinary issues surfacing for both teams, including yellow cards for Oualid Mhamdi , Patrick Mainka , and Julian Eitschberger . Dramatic conclusion Just as the game seemed to be settling into its closing stages, total chaos erupted. Deyovaisio Zeefuik was shown a straight red card in the 88th minute, leaving the hosts to battle with ten men. Capitalizing on the numerical advantage, 1. FC Heidenheim pushed forward with desperation. Their persistence paid off in the 90th minute when Oluwaseun Adewumi struck, latching onto a delivery from Josip Brekalo to finalize a thrilling comeback effort.
